JIT Compiler for dynamic code generation. Elysia has embedded JIT compiler since version 0.4 (30 Mar 2023) in src/compose.ts using new Function() or eval(). Not traditional compiler but dynamically generates optimized code for route handling. Generates code based on defined routes and middleware on first request. Avoids unnecessary overhead by only handling needed request parts. Static Code Analysis module Sucrose works alongside compiler at src/sucrose.ts.
Questions: What is Elysia's JIT compiler? How does it work? Why is it called JIT?

sections.manifest:
Sucrose static code analysis module. Reads handler code via Function.toString() performing custom pattern-matching. Extracts what request parts handler needs. Example: patch /user/:id with params-only handler - Sucrose tells compiler to parse only params, skip body/query/headers. Enables tailored request parsing.
Questions: What does Sucrose do? How does it extract handler requirements? What does it skip?

Compiler optimizations for performance. Various optimizations: control flow based on usage patterns, constant folding, direct property access vs iteration. Example optimizations: mapResponse, mapCompactResponse - constructing Response without status/headers cheaper than with. When set/status not used, mapCompactResponse used avoiding overhead.
Questions: What optimizations does compiler apply? What is mapCompactResponse?

Platform-specific optimizations for Bun, Node.js, Deno, Cloudflare Workers. Bun.serve.routes uses native Bun routing in Zig. Inline response for static responses. Bun.websocket for WebSocket. Bun.file for faster file handling. Headers.toJSON() for Bun header overhead reduction. Ranked #14 on TechEmpower Framework Benchmarks.
Questions: What platform-specific features are used? What is TechEmpower benchmark rank?

JIT compilation overhead. Initial request handling per route requires analysis and code generation - very fast usually < 0.005ms per route on modern CPU, happens once per route. Can be moved to startup via precompile: true for slower startup but no first-request overhead. Memory usage relatively low from dynamic code storage. Bundle size slightly increased from compiler/Sucrose code. Dynamic code generation increases codebase complexity and maintenance difficulty. Security: only trusts code generated by Elysia/Sucrose itself, input almost never user-controlled.
Questions: What is initial request overhead? How do you eliminate it? What security measures exist?

Libraries using eval: ajv (895m downloads/month), TypeBox (332m downloads/month) - industry standard validation libraries using eval for performance optimization. Elysia expands eval usage beyond validation to whole framework. Elysia also uses TypeBox internally.
Questions: Which validation libraries use eval? Why use eval for validation?

Opting out of JIT compilation. Set aot: false in Elysia constructor: `new Elysia({ aot: false })`. Disables JIT compilation entirely using dynamic mode. Not recommended - some features like trace missing without JIT.
Questions: How do you disable JIT? What features are missing without JIT?

Elysia performance achievements. Almost zero overhead - only limited by JavaScript engine speed. Extreme optimization trade-offs worth performance gains. Research paper published to ACM Digital Library about JIT compiler. Almost never saw valid benchmark where Elysia not fastest framework (except FFI/native bindings like Rust/Go/Zig). uWebSocket (C++ with JavaScript binding) outperforms in some cases despite serialization overhead.
Questions: How fast is Elysia compared to other frameworks? What limitations exist? Are there benchmarks?
